Diagnosis:
The failure stems from inefficiency and memory exhaustion triggered when fitting polynomial curves using the PolynomialFitter with the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer on large numbers of observed points (e.g., 40,000 points in the test). The current bug report indicates that when using the Weight class to pass a large number of weights to multivariate vector optimizers, an n×n full matrix is created and copied, which exponentially increases memory use and causes exhaustion for large n (number of data points or weights).

The failing testLargeSample() method generates a large dataset (40,000 points) and fits a polynomial model by invoking PolynomialFitter.fit(double[]) after adding observed points in a loop. The PolynomialFitter.fit(double[]) method delegates to fitting routines that eventually call the multivariate vector optimizer (LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer) under the hood. The large number of points results in a large system size and corresponding weights.

The crucial issue is that the Weight processing in the optimizer framework creates a full matrix for the vector of weights, which grows as the square of the number of points. This is unnecessary for diagonal weight matrices (one weight per observation) and causes memory exhaustion on large samples such as 40,000 points or more.

Since even low-degree polynomial fitting can have this problem due to many sample points, the test fails with memory issues. The underlying cause is a structural inefficiency introduced by the optimization weight handling that leads to full n×n matrices when only diagonal weighting is needed.

No relevant recent issues were found related to this problem, but the current bug report clearly highlights that the memory problem with weight handling affects curve fitting with large data sets using the multivariate vector optimizers used by PolynomialFitter.

Summary: The bug occurs because weights passed to the multivariate vector optimizers inside PolynomialFitter result in creation of huge full n×n matrices when large numbers of data points are used, exhausting memory. The failing test uses 40,000 points, triggering this inefficiency and failure.

Recommended method for fixes would involve the optimization of weight handling inside the optimizer or fitting classes to avoid building large full matrices for large numbers of weights, especially when diagonal weighting is sufficient.
